question.prompt: The function \(f\) satisfies the functional equation \[ f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)-xy-1 \] for every pair \(x,\) \(y\) of real numbers. If \(f(1)=1,\) then the number of integers \(n\ne1\) for which \(f(n)=n\) is

solutions.explanation:
Setting one input equal to 1 links values at consecutive integers, which is enough for this question. First, taking \(x=y=0\) gives
\[
2f(0)=f(0)-1,
\qquad f(0)=-1.
\]
Next, use \(y=1\) and \(f(1)=1\):
\[
f(x+1)=f(x)+x+2.
\]
In particular, the successive integer values have increments \(n+2\). Since these increments are linear in \(n\), look for a quadratic expression matching them. Define
\[
P(n)=\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2}.
\]
It has \(P(0)=-1\), and
\[
P(n+1)-P(n)=\frac{2n+4}{2}=n+2.
\]
Thus \(f(n)-P(n)\) is unchanged at every step from \(n\) to \(n+1\). Its value at 0 is zero. Moving forward or backward by integer steps proves that
\[
f(n)=\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2}
\]
for every integer \(n\), including negative integers.

Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)=n
&\iff n^2+n-2=0\\
&\iff(n-1)(n+2)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The only possibilities are \(n=1\) and \(n=-2\), and both satisfy the derived integer formula. Excluding 1 leaves exactly \(\boxed{1}\) integer, choice B.
solutions.title: Link consecutive integer inputs

solutions.explanation:
The term \(xy\) suggests subtracting a quadratic, because the expansion of \((x+y)^2/2\) contains exactly that mixed term. Define
\[
g(x)=f(x)-\frac{x^2}{2}+1.
\]
The functional equation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
g(x+y)-g(x)-g(y)
&=f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y)-xy-1\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)\) for all real inputs. Also,
\[
g(1)=1-\frac12+1=\frac32.
\]
Repeated addition shows that \(g(n)=3n/2\) for positive integers \(n\). The same identity gives \(g(0)=0\) and \(g(-n)=-g(n)\), so this formula holds for every integer. Therefore
\[
f(n)=\frac{n^2}{2}+\frac{3n}{2}-1.
\]
It follows that
\[
f(n)=n
\iff n^2+n-2=(n-1)(n+2)=0.
\]
The integer solutions are exactly \(1\) and \(-2\). After excluding 1, there is \(\boxed{1}\) qualifying integer, choice B.
solutions.title: Remove the mixed product
